note: Inputs for the serving roofline (SPEC v0.3 §6.6). Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so what a GPU delivers is a FUNCTION of the model being served — size, context, attention architecture and quantization — not a constant per accelerator. This file supplies the three tables that function needs. It ships NO throughput figures: every tok/s the calculator prints is derived from the formula and labelled at the point of use, so there is no unlabelled benchmark hiding in a data file.
accelerator_note: vram_gb is deliberately NOT duplicated here. It lives in gpu-pricing.json `gpus` and that stays the single source of truth — two copies of a capacity figure drift, and the copy that drifts is the one that silently mis-sizes a fleet. This file adds ONLY memory bandwidth, keyed by the same gpu_id.

h200.note: Same GH100 silicon as H100; HBM3e raises bandwidth.

h20.note: China-export Hopper: MORE bandwidth than H100 with far less compute, which is why it reads well on a bandwidth-bound decode model and poorly on prefill.

a800.note: NOT independently cited. A800 is the export-compliant A100 80GB: the NVLink interconnect is capped, the HBM2e stack is unchanged, so per-GPU bandwidth is taken as equal to a100_80. The cap affects multi-GPU scaling, which this model already discounts separately. Re-verify against a vendor datasheet before any figure derived from this row is quoted.

l40s.note: Ada, GDDR6 — no HBM, which is why it falls behind at long context despite competitive compute.

a10.note: 150W PCIe part sold by Azure and Alibaba. Same 24GB and same bandwidth as A10G; the parts differ in power and clocks.

l4.note: Half the bandwidth of A10G at the same 24GB.

bf16.label: BF16 / FP16 — full precision
bf16.note: The reference point. Two bytes per parameter is definitional, not an estimate.

fp8.label: FP8
fp8.note: Hopper and newer. Halves both the weight footprint and the bytes read per decode step.

int8.label: INT8 (W8A8)
int8.note: Same byte count as FP8; available on Ampere, which has no FP8 tensor cores.

int4.label: INT4 (AWQ / GPTQ)
int4.note: Quantized weights only. Real INT4 checkpoints carry unquantized embeddings, norms and scales, so the true footprint sits ABOVE this figure — the model understates INT4 VRAM and overstates INT4 throughput. Stated, not corrected: the correction factor is checkpoint-specific and inventing one would be worse than naming the bias.

fp8.label: FP8 KV cache
fp8.note: Halves KV bytes per token, which is the dominant term at long context.

runtime_note: [ASSUMED] — bandwidth_efficiency is the fraction of theoretical peak HBM bandwidth a decode step actually achieves. These are planning placeholders set by the site author on 2026-08-29, NOT measurements, and they are the single largest source of error in the derived throughput. They carry the assumed tag at every point of use and must never back a modelled_p95_capacity verdict (SPEC §6.5). Override with your own measurement.

tensor_parallel.note: [ASSUMED] — each GPU past the first contributes this fraction of a full GPU's bandwidth, compounding, to stand in for collective-communication overhead. Real scaling depends on interconnect: NVLink/NVSwitch holds up far better than PCIe, and the A800's capped NVLink is exactly the case this flat factor does not capture. A planning shape, not a measurement.

vram_overhead_fraction.note: [ASSUMED] — fraction of VRAM reserved for activations, CUDA graphs, allocator fragmentation and the runtime's own buffers, i.e. not available for weights or KV cache. The cited KV figures are LOGICAL cache; measured serving memory runs higher, and this fraction is the only thing standing in for that gap.

model_note: Every preset below reproduces a PUBLISHED per-token KV figure from the cited source, which itself verified each against the model's config.json. `kv_bytes_per_token_bf16_expected` is that published value: the test suite asserts the engine's own layer-group arithmetic lands on it exactly, so a formula error cannot ship silently. Layer groups are the general form — one flat layer count cannot express a hybrid, and the four architectures below are precisely the cases where a flat count is wrong.

models.label: Qwen3 8B — dense, full attention
models.note: The baseline case: every layer grows the cache and retains the whole context, so KV scales linearly with context length and dominates VRAM past ~8k.

models.label: Gemma 4 31B — sliding-window (5:1 local:global)
models.note: Sliding layers cost the SAME per stored token as full attention — what changes is retention: once the 1024-token window is full, an old entry leaves as a new one arrives, so those 50 layers stop growing while the 10 global layers keep scaling. The global layers use unified K=V, hence tensors:1 instead of 2. Window size 1024 is the large-model value from the Gemma 3 technical report (§2, 'a smaller span of only 1024 tokens to the local layers... 1 global for every 5 local'); small models use 512. params_b is read from the model name, not from a config file.

models.label: Qwen3-Next 80B-A3B — GDN hybrid, MoE
models.note: 48 decoder layers with full attention every fourth, so only 12 grow a KV cache; the 36 Gated DeltaNet layers add 0 B/token. Combined with 3B active of 80B resident, this is the configuration that separates VRAM cost from bandwidth cost most sharply — and the reason a per-accelerator throughput constant cannot represent it. state_bytes_per_seq is null and therefore UNMODELLED: the DeltaNet recurrent state is fixed in sequence length but nonzero, so VRAM for this model is understated by a constant per concurrent sequence. Named rather than guessed (SPEC §6.4).

models.label: DeepSeek V3 671B-A37B — MLA, MoE
models.note: Multi-head latent attention caches a compressed latent plus a rotary-key component, so the query-head count drops out of the per-token figure entirely: 61 x (512 + 64) x 2. A serving stack that expands the latent back into full K and V tensors has a different, larger footprint than this — the compact form is the architecture's claim, not every runtime's behaviour.

models.label: Custom — enter your own configuration
models.note: Starting shape only — every field is meant to be overwritten from your model's config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim). Nothing here is cited, and the calculator labels results from this preset accordingly.
